sections.title: Beat One — The Market
sections.subtitle: Arrival in Dunmore · Tamsin's empty stall · Meet Fanger · The marketplace breathes

content.text: Arrival in Dunmore
Dunmore is alive. Not in the precarious way of Hollowgate — alive in the way of a town that doesn't know it should be worried yet. The market runs full.

items: Fresh produce stacked in bright rows
A baker shouting prices over the noise
A blacksmith's hammer rhythm two streets over
Livestock being traded near the east gate
Children weaving between carts at full speed
Townsfolk greeting each other by name

content.text: This is the contrast that matters later. The market is healthy and ordinary and full of people who do not know what is growing at the edge of town.
Robyn's Role

Robyn is useful here without being the solution to anything. He can answer practical questions — where the general store is, which stalls sell food, where the blacksmith works, where common supplies are. Shopkeepers know him. He has a reputation for fair trades and unusual rocks.
"Robyn! Haven't seen you in a few weeks."
"Got any shiny rocks for me today?"
Some acknowledge him warmly. Some barely notice him. No one treats him like a local celebrity. He belongs here the way a regular traveler belongs — recognized, not famous.
Tamsin's Herbs & Garden

A stall near the center of the market bears a painted sign: Tamsin's Herbs & Garden. The stall is mostly packed up. A few empty crates remain. Nothing seems alarming. The neighboring vendor can explain:
"You just missed her. Packed up early today. Heat was getting to her."
Nothing about this seems unusual. Tamsin is simply another local merchant who left early. The stall is a thread — not yet a clue.

content.name: Who Tamsin Is — Through Other People

content.text: Introduce Tamsin through other people's warmth before the party knows she is dead. They should like her before they meet her.

items: "Auntie Tamsin? Sweetest woman in the market. Gives honey candies to children and lectures grown men about overwatering mint."
"She's been here twenty years. Knows every plant in the region by name."
"She always packs up at noon. Today was earlier."
"Plants were looking strange lately, though. Bigger than they should be."
"She seemed distracted this morning. Kept looking at the road."

content.text: Meet Fanger

Nearby, a market-goer is proudly showing off a small carnivorous plant they bought from Tamsin earlier that morning. The plant is about the size of a teacup — potted, covered in tiny leaves and small snapping mouths. Charming, even. Clearly purchased as a novelty.
"I call him Fanger."

If any player character gets too close, the plant snaps at their finger. 1 point of piercing damage. A small bead of blood appears. The plant's mouths seem unusually interested in it — orienting toward the hand before the blood is fully visible.
"See? Told you."
Most people find it amusing. The owner is proud. Let the scene breathe. This is not yet a warning — it is a novelty. The horror is in how ordinary it all seems.
One Person Isn't Laughing
One nearby vendor watches the Fanger demonstration with visible unease. They do not explain themselves readily. If the party notices and asks:
"Tamsin didn't think it was funny."
That is all they say right now. They do not elaborate. They go back to their stall.
This moment becomes significant after the Gourdmire Maw attack. Plant it now so it lands later.
Market Exploration
Give the players genuine time in the market. This is a shopping and roleplay opportunity — buy supplies, gather rumors, talk to merchants, identify herbs, meet Dunmore as a place.
Let them begin to forget about Fanger. Not completely. Just enough.
The longer the market exploration, the more effective the pumpkin attack. Do not rush this beat.

sections.title: Beat Two — The Gourdmire Maw
sections.subtitle: The pumpkin splits · Vines erupt · The marketplace becomes a disaster

content.text:
Shouting erupts from the far end of the market. People begin screaming. A crowd scatters. A produce cart overturns — cabbages rolling, a woman pulling her child backward, an old man frozen in the road.

A large pumpkin at the center of the cart begins to split.

Vines erupt outward.

The pumpkin unfolds.
The Encounter

The Gourdmire Maw is a serious encounter. It should feel dangerous. The marketplace is not a dungeon room — it is a living, endangered space. The party is protecting people, not simply fighting a monster.

items: Civilians in the direct path of the vines
Market stalls being destroyed as the creature moves
Animals panicking and pulling carts loose
Produce exploding underfoot as difficult terrain spreads
Children frozen in the middle of the street

content.text: Each round, introduce one complication. Every character should have an opportunity to contribute beyond attacking — protect someone, calm a horse, clear a path, pull someone free from rubble.
Round Complications

items: Civilian in Danger: A merchant trapped beneath a fallen stall. A child frozen in fear directly in the creature's path. An elderly shopper who cannot move fast enough.
Panicked Animal: A horse breaks free and bolts through the crowd. Livestock scatter and knock over neighboring stalls.
Property Damage: A stall collapses into the street and creates difficult terrain. Produce explodes underfoot. A cart overturns and blocks movement for the round.

content.text: Gourdmire Maw — Quick Reference

Medium Plant, Unaligned · A grotesque corruption of an ordinary pumpkin, dragging itself on thick vine-roots, splitting stalls as it moves. Its rind splits open into an impossibly wide mouth lined with jagged teeth and a long muscular tongue.
AC 13 (Thick Rind) · HP 55 · Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft.
Resistances: Piercing · Immunities: Charmed, Frightened

items: Rampaging Vines (passive): Difficult terrain within 10 ft. of the Maw.
Bite: +5 to hit, reach 10 ft. — 2d6+4 piercing. Medium or smaller: DC 13 STR save or Grappled.
Vine Lash: +5 to hit, reach 15 ft. — 1d8+3 bludgeoning. Target pulled 10 ft. toward the Maw.

Unhinging Maw (Recharge 5–6): Rind splits impossibly wide — nearly one and a half times the creature's own height. All within 10 ft.: DC 12 WIS save or Frightened until end of next turn. Immediately makes one Bite attack.

Rooted Fury (at 27 HP): The pumpkin shell cracks apart. Writhing roots burst through the rind. The players realize the pumpkin was only the fruiting body. AC rises to 15. Advantage on checks to maintain Grapples. Occurs once only.
Death Burst (on 0 HP): Body ruptures. Black seeds scatter 10 ft. DC 13 DEX save — Failure: 1d6 acid damage + Restrained by writhing vines until start of next turn.

sections.title: Beat Three — Following the Thread
sections.subtitle: Cart owner · Return to Fanger · The apothecary · The cottage marked on the map

content.text: The Cart Owner
The owner of the overturned produce cart is shaken. They are looking at what remains of their livelihood scattered across the street. When the party approaches:
"I bought that yesterday. It was just sitting there. It wasn't moving."

This is the critical detail. The creature did not arrive as a monster. It was purchased as ordinary produce and transformed afterward. The corruption is spreading through Tamsin's plants after they leave the greenhouse — sold before the change manifests.
Return to Fanger

When the party returns to the customer with the small carnivorous plant, the owner is no longer amused. They have seen the pumpkin attack. Fanger does not look charming anymore. When pressed, the full story comes out:
"Yesterday. Under the stall. Fanger bit something. I thought it was a rat."

But Tamsin had been there and seen it. She became visibly concerned. She immediately tried to buy the plant back — not for what the customer paid. For double. The customer refused. They thought she was joking, or regretting the sale.
"After that she just... got distracted. Kept looking at the plant. Then she packed up and left."
The uncomfortable vendor from earlier fills in now if pressed: "That's what I meant. Tamsin didn't think it was funny. She never thought the biting ones were funny."
The Apothecary
Any vendor in the market can point the party to the local apothecary. When they arrive and mention Tamsin's name, the apothecary recognizes it immediately.
"She was here earlier today."
What did she buy?
"Herbicide."
That should feel wrong. Nobody buys herbicide for healthy plants.

items: "She seemed worried. More worried than I've ever seen her."
"She didn't stop to talk. She just needed it and had to get home."
"She bought enough to treat a full greenhouse."
"I asked if she was alright. She said the plants were getting ahead of her."
"That's not something Tamsin says. She's been growing things in this town for twenty years."

content.text: The apothecary pauses. "You're going out there, aren't you." It is not quite a question. She takes the map, marks a spot east of the last proper houses on old orchard lane. "White cottage. Blue shutters. Big glasshouse behind it." She caps her ink. "Go before dark."
The apothecary's concern carries weight — she is a professional who knows Tamsin, and she recognized that Tamsin's worry was not ordinary.

sections.title: Beat Four — Tamsin's Overrun Cottage
sections.subtitle: The cart abandoned · The house claimed by growth · Hazards · Evidence · Her body

content.alt: Tamsin Vale's overgrown cottage with blue shutters and greenhouse behind
content.caption: Tamsin Vale — Herbs & Remedies · East of Dunmore · Old Orchard Lane

content.text: Arrival

content.name: The Cart. The House. The Wrong.

content.text: Tamsin's green-and-cream market cart sits crooked near the gate. One wheel cracked. The back hangs open. Butcher paper in the cart bed, dark with old blood. Roots have grown up through the wheels. The blue honey-candy tin spilled on the driver's bench.
Robyn goes quiet. "This is her cart. This is old plant-lady cart. She came home fast."

The cottage does not look ruined. Ruin would be simpler. Ivy covers the walls in overlapping sheets. The roof is buried under green growth. Lavender bundles beside the door have rooted into the wood and bloomed into impossible purple masses. The house has not collapsed. It has been planted.
The Drag Trail

content.name: Not in the Dirt — In the Plants

content.text: Roots have broken through the ground everywhere. A clean trail in the soil is impossible. Follow the damage through the plants instead:

items: Snapped ivy stems all bent the same direction
Broken branches with fresh leaves already regrowing around the wounds
A strip of blue cloth caught on a thorn
A smear of blood on the underside of a leaf — not the ground
Fertilizer spilled in a line toward the back hall
Roots pulled out of the soil where something struggled
A broken pruning basket

content.text: Cottage Hazards

Characters may move carefully through most of the house without rolling. The creepers trigger only when someone behaves carelessly or aggressively: rushing, forcing a blocked door, hacking at vines, raising fire, drawing a weapon aggressively, reaching into dense ivy, falling prone.

Effect: DC 11 Strength or Dexterity save or become Restrained. A restrained character can use an action to make a DC 11 check to escape. An adjacent ally frees them automatically using a blade carefully. Hacking wildly: 1d4 piercing. Accepting help: no damage.

The rats live in the walls and ivy. They do not attack freely. They wait for creatures that are restrained, prone, isolated, or distracted. They are testing whether the party is trapped enough to eat.

When a character is Restrained: DC 11 Dexterity save or 1d4 piercing. After any bite, they vanish back into the ivy and cannot be targeted without readied actions, area damage, or tearing open the hiding place.
Inside the Cottage

content.alt: The interior of Tamsin's cottage, overgrown with ivy and roots
content.caption: "Not darker. Greener."

content.text: Ivy covers the walls so completely that wallpaper is visible only in torn patches. Vines loop through chair backs, cabinet handles, and ceiling beams. Roots push up through the floorboards. Bags of fertilizer lie torn open near the kitchen door. Something small moves inside the ivy. Then it is gone.
What to Find
"Purchased today from a kobold trader. He believed it to be an egg. It is no egg, though I admit the resemblance is charming."
"The specimen responds to warmth, voice, and soil. The pulse is not a heartbeat exactly, but close enough to unsettle me."
"Meat calms the mouths, but not the heart."
"It is afraid. I am certain now. Not wild. Not wicked. Afraid."
"If I cut, it will learn that hands are teeth."
"I must reach it without blades. I must show it—"
A pair of pruning shears lies on the floor near the back hall. They are clean. Not bloodless — clean. Unused. Set aside deliberately.
Nearby note: "Do not cut living roots." This is one of the strongest solution clues in the house.

content.name: Sketch of Tamsin and Edrin Vale

content.text: On the wall, half-hidden beneath ivy: a framed charcoal sketch. A younger Tamsin kneels laughing in a garden bed, hands dark with soil. Beside her is a man with rolled sleeves and kind eyes, holding a crooked sapling upright while she packs earth around its roots. Behind them, the greenhouse stands new and bright.
"Our first spring under glass." The ivy has grown around the frame — not across it. Around it. Edrin Vale has been dead for years. The greenhouse was not just her business. It was her marriage.

A brass key on a hook by the back door, half-hidden under ivy. Tag reads: GLASSHOUSE — EAST LATCH. Opens one greenhouse door. Does not remove the briars. Lets the party enter quietly if they clear or calm the growth.
The Dead Patch and the Sprayer

content.alt: Brass herbicide sprayer beside a wall of blackened dead vines with gardening gloves on the floor
content.caption: Tamsin's gloves · The sprayer · 3 uses remaining

content.text: In the back hallway, a wide black stain spreads across one wall. The vines within it are shriveled and brittle, curled into themselves like fingers in a fire. Leaves crumble underfoot. The air smells sharp and chemical beneath the wet earth scent.

On the floor: Tamsin's thick gardening gloves, patched at the thumb, stained with soil and green-gold sap. Beside them: a brass-and-glass sprayer, tank half-full, nozzle uncapped. The living ivy grows around the dead area but does not enter it. Roots approach the edge, then curl away.
The party already knows she bought herbicide from the apothecary. Now they see what she did with it — and that she stopped.
If Hypha is present: she feels a pulse from deeper in the house — pain · bitter rain · old hands shaking · green going silent · do not let them spray again.

3 uses remaining. As an action, spray a plant creature or living plant hazard within 15 feet: 1d8 necrotic damage, plus 2 necrotic at the start of its next turn. Can also clear a 5-foot patch of creepers or root growth.
Each use increases the greenhouse's panic by 1 unless used only on already-dead growth. After Hypha bonds with the Heart Seed, plant damage reflects onto her — the sprayer becomes catastrophic.

Advantage on checks to carefully handle non-hostile plant growth, remove vines from objects, or retrieve items from creepers without provoking them. The gloves do not allow safe retrieval of the Heart Seed — that requires trust, not gloves.
Tamsin's Final Note

content.name: Found Near Her Body or in Her Hand

content.text:
"The mouths are hungry, but the heart is afraid.

Do not burn.

Do not cut.

Do not carry it like a thing.

Let it know your hands before you lift it."
This is the final encounter key written in Tamsin's voice. It should be the last thing the party finds before entering the greenhouse.
Tamsin's Body

Pale creepers have wrapped around her shoulders, waist, and legs. Not like predators feeding. Like frightened hands holding her still. One hand reaches toward the greenhouse. The other rests near the pruning shears she chose not to use. Tiny white flowers have bloomed around her throat and wrists.
The plants killed her. But they also protected her body. That detail keeps the greenhouse morally complicated. She was not trying to destroy it. She simply ran out of time.
Robyn at the Cottage
Robyn recognizes the candy tin. He goes quiet when he sees the body. He sold her the seed. He believed it was a fair trade. Now he sees what the trade cost.
"Robyn gave her seed. Robyn did not know it would bite her."
"This is not good trade. This is bad trade forever."
Do not play this as guilt-trip comedy. Play it as a genuine beat. He stays quiet for a while.

sections.title: Beat Five — The Greenhouse
sections.subtitle: A living dungeon · Rings of fear · Communion · The seed goes with Hypha

content.alt: The overgrown greenhouse interior with carnivorous plants and the Heart Seed glowing at center
content.caption: Tamsin's Glasshouse · The Heart Seed's cage · Every plant in the room leans toward it

content.text: Overview

The greenhouse has reorganized itself into defensive rings around the buried Heart Seed — briars at the entrance, a lure path of false voices and sticky ground, hunger beds of carnivorous plants, strangling root curtains, and a heartroot cage at the center.

The party begins treating it as a combat encounter. That is reasonable. But new growth sprouts every round. The party cannot kill their way through. Fighting harder makes it worse. The lesson arrives early.

Once Hypha reaches the Heart Seed and touches it, the encounter changes. She enters a fear communion. From that point forward, any damage dealt to a living plant creature or hazard also deals half that damage to Hypha. The party must stop attacking and help her feel safe enough to calm the seed.
The final victory is not killing the greenhouse. It is making it believe them.
The Correct Answer

items: Drop or sheathe weapons
Extinguish all open flame
Step back, open empty hands, speak softly
Robyn kneels and apologizes
Someone reads Tamsin's final note aloud
Promise not to take the seed from Hypha
Offer water, soil, or open sky
Let Hypha decide what happens next

content.text: The seed does not speak. It is not ready for that. But it goes with Hypha willingly. This is a first meeting, not a recovery. Neither of them fully understands what it is yet.
The seed will not introduce itself until approximately level 7. Its name will reflect Hypha's destiny. They are both still becoming.

sections.title: Hypha's Reveal — Party Perception Checks
sections.subtitle: Let the battle breathe first · Three staged outside observations · Not hinted early

content.text: How These Work

These checks are made by the party — triggered when players adjacent to Hypha look her way or interact with her during the chaos. They give the outside view of something Hypha is experiencing from the inside simultaneously. The full internal experience is detailed in the greenhouse encounter reference.
The GM does not hint at any of this early. Let the battle breathe. Let resources drain. The revelation emerges from what is already visible.
The GM never says "the seed is calling her." The GM describes what Hypha's body is doing before her mind catches up. She is already moving toward the center.

content.label: Perception Check — Absence of Attacks
content.timing: Surfaces when the party has been fighting long enough to notice who is and isn't taking damage.

content.text: On success: "None of the plants have attempted to attack Hypha."
This can be dismissed as luck. As positioning. As Hypha staying clear. Plant the observation and let it sit.

content.label: Perception Check — Active Defense
content.timing: A round or two later, after someone has gone down or used a major resource.

content.text: On success: "The plants nearest to Hypha have had extra attacks — toward the rest of you. They are not ignoring her. They are defending her."
This is the reframe. Not luck. Not positioning. The greenhouse is protecting her. This is when the player's stomach drops.

content.label: Perception Check — The Call
content.timing: When the party is on the edge and Hypha is beginning to feel something she cannot name.

content.text: On success: "They answer the seed's call. The seed is calling her."
By the time the third check lands, everyone at the table knows what Hypha has to do. Nobody needs to be told.
Once the call is understood, the party is no longer trying to win a fight. They are trying to buy someone time to do something they cannot do themselves.

sections.title: The Hold — Three Rounds
sections.subtitle: Hypha takes the seed · Feels what it has felt · The greenhouse stills

content.text: Hypha Reaches the Center

The plants part for Hypha as she moves toward the center. They do not attack her. They close behind her. The path seals. The party cannot follow without fighting through — the plants still attack everyone else.
When she takes the Heart Seed, she cannot act for three rounds. She is not meditating. She is holding something that is terrified, and it is showing her what it remembers.
The party protects her. The greenhouse is still fighting. This is the most dangerous part of the encounter for everyone except Hypha.
The Transition

The leshy's hand closes around the Heart Seed.

For one breath, the greenhouse goes silent.

No vines move. No flowers bite. No rats scratch in the walls.

The seed pulses once in her palm.

Then her eyes widen.

Then every plant in the greenhouse turns toward the party.

content.label: Round One — Fear
content.mechanic: WIS Save (DC 14) · Failure: Frightened until end of next turn · Greenhouse at full intensity
content.feel: The seed's first memory is the theft — roots torn, something wrong, the world suddenly not the way it was. The violation of being taken. Hypha absorbs it as raw terror that is not her own. The fear passes through her like a current. The plants spike into aggression as the seed's panic spikes.

content.label: Round Two — Grief
content.mechanic: 2d6 Psychic Damage · The greenhouse begins to slow — still dangerous, but plants show first signs of uncertainty
content.feel: The next memory is Tamsin. Old hands. Wet earth smell. Someone who knew how to tend things. The seed felt hope — briefly, genuinely — and then the warm presence stopped. It only knows: the warmth ended, and the ending was connected to its hunger. Hypha feels the loneliness of a frightened thing that watched someone die because of it.

content.label: Round Three — Recognition
content.mechanic: No damage · The seed feels Hypha back · The greenhouse stills
content.feel: Something shifts. The seed stops remembering and starts feeling. It feels Hypha. Not as a threat. Not as a captor. As the thing it has been calling toward since before it knew it was calling. The greenhouse quiets. One by one, the plants ease back. The room, for the first time in days, breathes.

content.text: The seed does not speak. It is not ready for that. But it goes with Hypha willingly. This is a first meeting — not a recovery. The relationship between them is just beginning.
The seed will not introduce itself until approximately level 7. Its name will reflect Hypha's destiny. Neither of them knows that name yet. They are both still becoming.

sections.title: Robyn's Moment — Not Good Trade
sections.subtitle: The weight lands · Bad trade forever · Where Robyn becomes real

content.text: Robyn has been treating the sale as an unfortunate misunderstanding. He found a buyer. Good price. No stabbing. He did not steal anything. He was told to sell it and he sold it. That is not failure. That is completing the task.
The open door. The broken basket. The blue candy tin spilled on the driver's bench. Robyn is quiet. He does not make jokes. He recognizes the candy tin.
"Old plant-lady was nice."

He sold her the seed. He does not know the chieftain's choice, the forest's design, the Concord's conspiracy. He knows only that there is an old woman lying beneath white flowers with her hand still reaching for the center, and he was the one who gave her what killed her.
"Robyn gave her seed. Robyn did not know it would bite her."
"This is not good trade. This is bad trade forever."
"Robyn wants to fix. Robyn does not know how. But Robyn wants."

Robyn watches Hypha hold the seed. He watches the greenhouse still. He understands that the party kept their word — they said they would find the seed and they found it. They said they would let him come and they let him come. That is new to him. He does not know what to do with it yet. But he notices.

conclusion.title: GM Summary — Running This Arc
items: The market sequence establishes Dunmore as a living, healthy place before it becomes a crisis zone. Do not rush Beats One through Three — the longer the players settle in, the more effective the Gourdmire Maw attack will be.

Tamsin should feel warm and loved before the party ever meets her. Every vendor line, every mention of honey candy and basil arguments, is load-bearing. When they find her body, they should already feel the loss.

Fanger is not immediately alarming. It should feel like a novelty act. The uncomfortable vendor's one line — 'Tamsin didn't think it was funny' — is a seed that only flowers after the Gourdmire Maw fight.

The Gourdmire Maw is a disaster encounter, not a dungeon fight. Every round should introduce a civilian, animal, or property complication. Players should feel like they are managing a crisis, not clearing a room.
The thread through Beat Three runs in any order: cart owner → Fanger owner → apothecary. All three roads lead to the cottage. Let players find them naturally.
The apothecary is the map-provider and carries more weight than a simple trade connection — she is someone who knew Tamsin well enough to recognize that worry was out of character for her.

The cottage is a dungeon in miniature. Creepers restrain careless characters. Rats attack only the restrained. The herbicide sprayer is available but has consequences. Everything points toward the same solution: do not cut, do not burn, let it know your hands.
The greenhouse cannot be won by killing. Let the combat teach them. Do not make it obvious.

The three perception checks give the party the outside view. They run alongside Hypha's internal experience detailed in the encounter reference. The GM never announces that Hypha is not being attacked — the party figures it out.
The hold is three rounds of the party being the most important people in the room while solving nothing. They buy time. Hypha resolves it. That gap is the emotional core of the encounter.
Tamsin's body should land quietly. No dramatic announcement. They find her beneath white flowers, hand still reaching.
Robyn goes quiet at the cart and stays quiet through the greenhouse. Let the player feel it without narrating it.
After the hold, the seed goes with Hypha. The arc does not end here — it begins here.
